/* Compose only authored prefixes. Both preserve native local 1 and have the
 * same 19-local type signature, so no game instructions need rewriting. */
'use strict';
const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path'),assert=require('node:assert/strict');
function locals(bytes){let p=0;const u=()=>{let n=0,s=0,x;do{x=bytes[p++];n|=(x&127)<<s;s+=7}while(x&128);return n>>>0};const groups=u(),types=[];for(let i=0;i<groups;i++){const n=u(),t=bytes[p++];for(let j=0;j<n;j++)types.push(t);}return {end:p,types};}
function compose(car,wall){const a=locals(car),b=locals(wall);assert.deepEqual(a.types,b.types,'contact prefixes must share the same full local signature');assert.equal(a.types.length,19);assert.equal(a.types[0],127);assert.equal(car.at(-1),11);assert.equal(wall.at(-1),11);return [...car.slice(0,-1),...wall.slice(b.end)];}
module.exports={compose,locals};

#!/usr/bin/env python3
from pathlib import Path
import argparse, hashlib, json, zipfile
root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
source = root / 'extension'
manifest = json.loads((source / 'manifest.json').read_text())
assert manifest['version'] == '0.30.0'
folder = 'NFSU2-Driving-Tools-v0.30.0'
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path)
args = parser.parse_args()
out = args.output or root.parent / 'NFSU2-Driving-Tools-v0.30-Combined-Info-HUD.zip'
files = ['README.md', 'CHANGELOG.md', 'manifest.json', 'popup.html', *manifest['content_scripts'][0]['js']]
assert len(files) == len(set(files))
assert sorted(files) == sorted(p.name for p in source.iterdir() if p.is_file())
assert all((source / p).is_file() for p in files)
assert manifest['content_scripts'][0]['matches'] == ['https://nfsu2.xyz/*']
assert manifest['content_scripts'][0]['world'] == 'MAIN'
# Exclusive creation keeps any previously delivered archive immutable.
with zipfile.ZipFile(out, 'x', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=9) as z:
    for name in files:
        # Canonical metadata makes the same reviewed sources reproduce the same ZIP.
        entry = zipfile.ZipInfo(folder + '/' + name, date_time=(1980, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0))
        entry.create_system = 3
        entry.external_attr = 0o100644 << 16
        entry.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
        z.writestr(entry, (source / name).read_bytes(), compress_type=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=9)
with zipfile.ZipFile(out) as z:
    assert z.testzip() is None
    assert len(z.namelist()) == len(files)
    for name in files:
        assert z.read(folder + '/' + name) == (source / name).read_bytes()
print(json.dumps({'path': str(out), 'size': out.stat().st_size, 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(out.read_bytes()).hexdigest(), 'files': files}, indent=2))

# NFSU2 Driving Tools: experimental v0.33.0

Unpacked Chrome / Edge / Brave extension for https://nfsu2.xyz/. See `CHANGELOG.md` for this release's changes and verification limits.

## v0.33.0: Continuous adaptive corner targets

Adaptive road-race speed now has a separate native planning command. Every valid sampled nonzero bend receives a smooth curvature-based target, instead of requiring it to cross the older curvature threshold. Exact straights keep the requested target ceiling; existing native lower/stop results are never increased. The native distance-based braking calculation uses the same pace compensation.

The curve is deliberately conservative and experimental. It does not detect every corner on the map: the native planner may provide no corner records, skip a tail record, report zero curvature or use another route. It does not change steering, physical brakes, route lookahead, NOS or other cars. A hook hit is an observation of a past call, not proof the current corner is safe. Five fresh captures show hook hits despite reported missed turns, so the update is not presented as a proven fix for every failure.

Only adaptive road mode uses this new command. **Street X and existing free-roam/road-corner controls retain their exact prior behavior.** The new command also denies actual/forced Street X and known online Street X in its native guards. AI ownership, native handback, online permission, mode checks and watchdog remain required. This does not bypass an AI failure or acquire control automatically.

The option remains default-off/session-only and uses your current sliders without changing saved values. For the first comparison, try the existing defaults: 1.30× adaptive ceiling, 0.80 corner factor and 0.75 braking factor. Higher targets can still cause missed turns. The latest logs used 1.90×, 0.95 and 1.00 respectively; those settings were confirmed, not shown to be safe. Keep the working Street X setup unchanged.

Corner/braking hit counters now use the existing two-second telemetry sample cadence instead of replacing bounded history every quarter second. Discrete control/mode changes still log promptly. No raw route geometry, memory dump or additional personal data is collected.

Native tests execute the new corner and braking hooks against the pinned game routines, compare legacy commands byte-for-byte, and check protected outputs and guard denials. Live cornering, race results and browser rendering remain unverified. The final combined suite passes **1,942 tests, zero failures/skips/cancellations**. All four supported patched modules compile, with only the two reviewed corner/braking wrapper functions changed from v0.32.

## Retained v0.32.0: Race-only automatic driver

In **AI driver**, enable **Race-only automatic driver** to arm the native driver for races you start or join yourself. It waits for the active race/GO state, includes Street X, Drag and Drift, and requests handback in free roam, outrun, results or other ineligible contexts. It does not find, join, start, replay or vote for events.

The existing **Automatic driver** still includes free roam. Selecting either driver mode turns the other off. The race-only switch is **off by default**, stays armed between races on this page, and resets on page reload or profile Load. It is deliberately not added to saved profiles; existing saved choices and storage remain unchanged.

**F7, F9/Stop, or driving-key takeover during a race disarms race-only AI.** Manual steering in free roam leaves it armed. If driving controls are still physically held when entering a race, acquisition waits until they are released. Turning the switch off requests native handback. A genuine native manual request, finished/totaled state, failed-control latch or watchdog is not forced back to AI.

Online races still need the existing **Allow network tools** permission. Exact build, current ownership, race, focus/menu, native driver and handback guards are retained. A selected switch is not proof of active ownership; the HUD and local log show the effective request and native observations separately.

Optional **Adaptive road-race speed** is also included below. It remains off by default and leaves Street X unchanged. Neither option changes steering, shifting, NOS or game saves. Live race efficacy and browser appearance remain unverified.

**Historical v0.32 verification:** that release passed **1,907 automated tests, zero failures/skips/cancellations**, including race-only eligibility/lifecycle, optional adaptive mode, joint Street X/online/stop behavior and all retained features. Independent tests additionally cover production native handback and cached-route reconstruction. At v0.32, all four supported patched game module outputs were byte-identical to v0.31; v0.33 changes only the two planner wrappers described above.

For an existing installation, replace matching files in the already loaded extension folder, click **Reload** on that extension's browser card, then refresh the game. Verify **0.33.0**. Do not remove/re-add the extension or create a different folder just for this update.

## Optional adaptive road-race speed

A new **default-off, session-only** option coordinates the existing native route planner. Its separate straight-target ceiling defaults to **1.30×** and ranges from 1.00× to 2.00×. The native route uses distance to known corners to lower its target in advance while retaining a higher target on sufficiently long straights. This is a planned target factor, not a physical speed cap or a measured speed increase.

Enable either **Race-only automatic driver** or **Automatic driver**, then **Adaptive road-race speed** in AI driver → Road-race settings. Online use also requires **Allow network tools**. Adaptive mode uses the existing Race corner speed, Race sharp-turn margin and Race braking factor values, even when the separate Road-race hairpin assist switch is off. Lower braking factor requests earlier braking. It overrides the effective custom race pace only in eligible ordinary road races, without changing any saved switch or slider.

**Street X keeps the exact existing pace, corner and braking selections.** Adaptive mode is dormant in actual/forced Street X and the known online Street X mode. Drag, Drift/forced variants, Outrun and free roam are also excluded. Selecting adaptive mode does not turn on Automatic driver or network permission.

The optional ceiling stays constant while driving. The existing native route envelope varies by distance; JavaScript does not switch pace or reconstruct the driver at every corner. A deliberate setting or race-mode change may still require the existing OFF/acknowledgement/ON route reconstruction. Manual takeover, race end, permission withdrawal and the existing watchdog remain in force.

F7/manual driving keys stop AI and leave the optional selection dormant. F9/Stop, profile Load and page reload turn adaptive mode off. It is not added to saved tool profiles or legacy session preferences. Blur, hidden page and menus pause it normally. Turn it off to return to the prior controls after native handoff.

The HUD and local log distinguish a request, matching native pace acknowledgement, and observed corner/braking hook evidence. These counters do not measure braking success, safe corner entry or a clean lap. There is no new steering, obstacle avoidance, NOS control, added route horizon, opponent manipulation or collision protection. Higher targets can still cause crashes. Start at 1.30× and assess one change at a time.

The original v0.32 option used page orchestration only. The v0.33 continuous-corner update changes the two native planner wrappers and teaches the controller a separate adaptive command. Existing planner commands retain their prior behavior; engine tuning, NOS, Drag-retention, tuner and saved-profile implementations are untouched. Exact-native synthetic tests support the route-speed envelope; live racing, lap times, wins and browser layout remain unverified.

## Retained v0.31.0: Keep owned Drag AI through settings refreshes

It does not acquire new control, force a real manual request back to AI, or change steering, shifting, NOS or damage.

A separate fix ensures a pause/end/OFF command is acknowledged by the native game before a quick restart can overwrite it. This also covers consecutive matches that reuse the same player, car and race objects. It does not clear the game's failed-control latch while AI remains continuously requested.

**F7/manual takeover, F9/OFF, native finish/totaled states, permission withdrawal, identity changes and the 180-native-frame watchdog remain effective.** Do not use this as a no-crash, no-damage or guaranteed-win feature. Online use still requires the existing explicit Allow network tools opt-in.

The fresh user log shows a request for manual Drag before the observed handback, matching the reproduced ordering. It does not record the rejecting guard, so this is not proof of that run's exact cause. The log came from v0.28. Live handoff prevention remains unverified.

## Retained v0.30.0: Compact driving information HUD

A small, click-through **Info HUD** appears below the upper-right launcher while the tools menu is closed. **F6** toggles it, or open **F8 → Info HUD**. It starts on and remembers only its display choice in this tab, separately from driving-tool profiles. Opening the menu hides the card until you close it. F7 returns control and F9 still stops driving assists; the HUD itself never enables them.

- **Speed:** existing guarded native speed converted to **km/h**. Zero is shown only when sampled as zero. Unknown builds, invalid car data and paused/missing samples show **Unavailable**, never a guessed or multiplied speed. Older supported builds without verified speed telemetry also show Unavailable.
- **Driver:** observed native AI/manual state, pending handoff, or the reason tools are waiting/paused. A selected AI switch is not called active by itself.
- **Pace:** `req` is the current requested AI target factor; `ack` is a matching native acknowledgement, not measured vehicle speed. A newly selected factor does not reuse an old acknowledgement. Selected pace waits for AI; Drag and Drift retain native pace.
- **Power:** `req` is the selected field multiplier; `set` reports guarded power-field application. It is not measured horsepower or a guaranteed speed increase. Paused, rejected and settling states stay distinct from application.

The HUD is read-only and uses existing observations. Stop, manual takeover, blur, hidden tab, game exit, replacement boot and tuner suspension clear old display evidence. No new physics, AI, speed/power formula, native hook, network permission, tuning, game-save or profile-schema change is included. The complete v0.29 tuner/static-ride fix, online NOS correction, Street X, Drift, Drag and online tools remain together.

## Retained v0.29.0: Accept verified native car records in the tuner

Arbitrary low addresses remain rejected; the existing heap path and all other safety checks remain.

## Retained v0.28.0: Correct the online Unlimited NOS clock

Unlimited NOS now refreshes an already-active NOS timestamp using the same clock the native game selected. The previous version always used the world clock; in an online fixture where the game's real clock was ahead, that made a full kit immediately appear depleted and caused repeated native stop/restart cycles. The corrected code retains the burst in that exact native test.

This is a reproduced timing defect, **not proof of the clock values in your live run or a guarantee that NOS never stops**. Native AI can still cancel NOS for normal driving decisions. This update does not hold Alt, force activation, suppress native stops or change driving, shifting, steering or lane choice. Inactive and sentinel timestamps remain inactive; network permission and current-car/kit checks remain mandatory.

For an online comparison, use the same ordinary driving situation with **Unlimited NOS** and **Allow network tools** enabled. If tapping remains, use **Export crash log** immediately. The new log samples the selected clock, active-since stamp and kit/resource accounting **before refill**; it contains no pointers. The timestamp flag does not prove successful activation, and sampled logs can miss short transitions.

The v0.28 combined suite passed **1,740 tests, zero failures/skips/cancellations**. Saved tool profiles, working Street X behavior, reviewed Drift isolation, Drag protection, online collision/corner settings and the full tuner with snapshot diagnostics remain together. No native game code or profile was changed. v0.28 did not change tuner capture. The v0.29 native-record correction is described above; any remaining rejection still needs its S-code/log. Live NOS behavior and game-save persistence remain unverified.

## Retained v0.25.0: Saved extension settings profiles

Update replaces the selected saved configuration; Delete removes it. These profiles are separate from the game's race tuning presets and **Save Profile**. They contain no car setup, game save, dyno draft or diagnostic log.

Automatic loading after reload is **optional and off by default**. Select it explicitly for a saved configuration if you want that configuration to return next time. Network permission has a separate saved-profile opt-in: saved choices do not silently grant Online/LAN access. Read the network warning before permitting automatic network-enabled behavior. Each tool still requires the supported build, valid current car and its normal game-mode checks.

**F9 / Stop keeps saved profiles but pauses automatic loading persistently**, as well as clearing current driving/network choices. A later reload cannot silently undo Stop. Resume deliberately from the profile controls. Saving a profile does not itself enable its settings. Changes from another tab do not automatically activate a configuration in an already-open tab.

Profile loading stops the old controllers and releases synthetic input before changing selections. It does not roll back a staged game tune or save the game. If storage is unavailable or full, the UI reports that the profile was not saved. Profiles stay in this browser; clearing this site's storage removes them, and site scripts can access this storage. Up to 16 profiles and 48 characters per name are supported. Browser-managed locking prevents concurrent tabs from overwriting each other's saves; if locking is unavailable, profile editing is disabled while manual loading remains available.

Saved Drag blowout protection retains its narrow meaning: only the current eligible local engine is protected before it blows; online use also needs network permission. It does not revive an already-blown engine, alter NOS/shifting, or promise a race win. Existing controls keep their normal fresh-page defaults unless you explicitly enable a saved startup profile. Descriptions below that say a control starts off refer to those defaults.

No native AI, Street X, tuning, heat, corner/braking or collision payload was changed for settings profiles. The final suite passes 1,688 tests, with another 44 independent profile checks. A local Chromium fixture could not launch because this environment denied socket creation, so browser appearance and automatic loading in the user's game remain unverified.

## Retained v0.24.0: Opted-in online Drag engine blowout protection

For **online or LAN Drag**, enable both **Drag racing → Disable Drag engine blowouts** and **Online / LAN opt-in → Allow network tools** before the engine blows. Solo Drag needs only the blowout toggle. Exact **93af6ccb** and **78e2bb69** builds are supported. The heat toggle works independently of Automatic driver and Manual drag assist. It starts off for a fresh tab, remembers your choice in the same tab, and F9 clears it. Network permission starts off after reload and F9.

Only the current linked local player's engine is eligible, during active Drag with full physics. Opponent, stale, unowned, invalid and already-blown engines remain excluded. This is local protection, not a change to remote engines, network packets or server rules. Follow server rules; online changes can trigger integrity checks or sanctions.

Enable it **before** the engine blows. It does not repair an already-blown engine or reverse a lost race. While enabled it supplies the game's own disabled-heat sentinel, intentionally discarding accumulated heat. Turning it off resumes normal heating from zero after the next native full-physics setup. It does not change shifts, throttle, steering, pace, power, torque, limiter, NOS decisions or opponents, and does not trigger an AI restart.

The exact native heat routine and its original instructions remain intact. An authored prefix checks active Drag, current player/car/race/engine identity, full physics, finite unblown heat, permission epoch and heartbeat before changing only the current engine's heat field. Online/LAN additionally requires literal network permission. Added diagnostics show bounded heat/blown/limit observations and the requested toggle.

Controlled native tests cover 600 online over-redline updates on each supported module, low and high runtime CPU addresses, opt-out restoring native heating and rejected ownership/stale states. This is **not live online verification**. A fresh race must still confirm the guard is eligible and the engine remains protected; a selected checkbox alone does not prove activation. No successful live Drag race, HUD appearance or win is claimed. Repeated native NOS cycling is unchanged.

This stays combined with the complete preset tuner, opted-in online corner/braking settings and local online race-car filtering. Solo/Street X driving formulas remain unchanged. No Lap Knockout experiment or unverified native grip/downforce multiplier is enabled.

## Signature scanning and build updates

The loader performs a read-only scan against three reviewed sets of 34 typed function fingerprints. It reports unique, ambiguous and missing matches in local diagnostics, plus the actual module hash. The menu retains the full compatibility explanation rather than truncating it. AI and Dyno now give the same explicit unavailable-build reason instead of suggesting the wrong tuning screen.

**Signature matches do not automatically authorize a new game version.** Matching functions alone do not establish callees, dispatch tables, host addresses, scratch ownership or live behavior. Even 34/34 matches on a different binary leave tools disabled until an exact compatibility profile has been reviewed. This is update diagnosis, not a promise that future game updates will work automatically. Scanner failure does not override the independent exact-binary gate.

## Automatic AI race-type switching

Turn on **AI driver → Automatic driver** once per page. It automatically selects:

- **Non-drag races and free roam:** the existing native player autopilot.
- **Drag:** experimental native racer AI with the verified drag physics type. It waits until GO and full driving physics are available.
- **Changing mode:** requests native AI OFF, waits for the game thread to acknowledge it, confirms ownership is released, the human driver is restored and any failed-acquisition latch is cleared, then requests the new mode. Player, car, race, track, drag/drift/URL/StreetX flags, forced native mode flags and race/free-roam changes are checked, including when object pointers are reused.

There is no separate drag-AI checkbox. The main switch explicitly enables automatic selection, including experimental drag. **You still start events yourself. This does not select races, restart them, navigate career menus, buy upgrades or choose a GPS destination.** It includes the separate experimental free-roam corner-speed and dyno-search tools described below. They are off by default.

The extension requests the game's native player autopilot, not a new steering bot. The native constructor chooses a distinct drift behavior and a shared ordinary/drag/StreetX behavior; its update code contains drag-specific branches. Circuit, sprint, URL and outrun do not have separately proven opponent-equivalent implementations here. The player racer identity stays unchanged. “Level 9” means the ordinary native skill field is set to 9; values 254/255 are preserved. We have not proved that drag's launch, shifting or lane decisions consume that field.

**Live drag driving remains unverified.** Correct driver/physics status does not prove that it shifts, steers, avoids traffic or finishes. It may crash, stop or miss checkpoints. Back up your progress and test solo first. No guaranteed routes, perfect drift, wins or completed races.

### Quick start

1. Back up your save with the game's **Download backup** button.
2. Keep your previous extension folder for rollback. Disable its extension card before loading this version.
3. Extract this ZIP. In `chrome://extensions` (Edge: `edge://extensions`), enable Developer mode and choose **Load unpacked**. Select **NFSU2-Driving-Tools-v0.29.0**, containing `manifest.json`.
4. Reload the game and check version **0.29.0**. Only one version should be enabled.
5. Start a solo event yourself. Open Driving tools with **F8**, then enable **Automatic driver** in a non-drag event. For your first drag test, leave power, grip, NOS, custom pace, collision filters and manual Drag assist off.
6. Enter other supported events normally. AI requests native handback/reconstruction automatically when the event changes. Turn AI off before using manual drag assist. Other selected settings are kept.

Chrome 111+ or a compatible current Chromium browser is required. This is not a Firefox or mobile-browser build. No build tools or Node installation are needed to install the extension.

### Take control and pause

- **F7 / Take control:** disables automatic AI until you explicitly turn it on again. Arrow/WASD keys and Space also take control outside the extension menu. This remains off across later race-type changes.
- Controller axes do not trigger takeover; use F7 or the Take control button.
- Taking control also pauses synthetic manual-drag throttle until you toggle manual Drag assist again.
- **F9 / Stop:** clears automatic AI, all four collision switches, Online/LAN permission, custom pace, NOS, power, limiter, grip and manual drag. Slider values are retained. Drift and the read-only tester keep their own switches.
- Menus, loading, unfocused/hidden tabs and unsupported states pause tools without clearing choices. They resume when a supported driving state returns, unless you took manual control.
- **Automatic AI, wall pass-through, solo car no-clip, online traffic no-clip, corner assist, both pace opt-ins, power boost, limiter removal, extra grip, dyno tuner and Online/LAN permission start OFF after every page reload.** Other settings use same-tab session storage. Closing the tab normally ends those saved choices. Storage may be unavailable or affected by browser restore behavior.
- If the page stops updating, native AI hands back within 180 game frames. A frozen game cannot process a handback. Disable the extension and reload if it freezes.

## Compact menu

The menu starts as a **170 × 29 px** collapsed toolbar and opens to a **244 px** drawer with a 390 px maximum scroll panel. **F8** opens/closes it. Sections start folded, only one main section opens at a time, and longer sections scroll. Help and detailed status are tucked away; no control was removed. **F7 / Take control** and **F9 / Stop** remain keyboard shortcuts, with buttons in the open toolbar.

## Independent controls

### AI and pace

The native AI switch uses player-only skill **9**, the highest normal native value. It restores the original value when the same racer still exists. Special sentinels are left unchanged and are not claimed as level 9. It does not alter other racers or commandeer an AI driver the extension did not acquire.

**Free-roam pace:** 0.75×–3.00× for native free roam only, default off / 1.00×. Its factor is saved, but its switch starts off after reload.

**Race / outrun pace:** a separate 0.75×–3.00× opt-in, default off / 1.00×. Its value is saved, but its switch starts off after reload. Your faster free-roam choice does not carry into races.

Both adjust the native target-speed factor, not engine power, steering or road paths. **2–3× pace is especially experimental: severe overspeed, missed turns/checkpoints and instability are possible.** No real driving at those factors has been verified. Drag, dyno and unknown categories use neutral 1.00×. The choices remain selected while ineligible and resume only in their own category. F7 leaves them dormant; F9 clears both switches. They never turn AI on by themselves.

### Free-roam corner-speed assist

A separate, experimental opt-in reduces the native planner's curvature-limited speed for upcoming free-roam corners. It does not replace steering or road paths. Its bounded factor is **0.60–0.95**, starting at **0.80**. Straight/gentle segments retain their native speed cap. This factor is a tuning hypothesis, not a measured optimum.

**Sharp-turn margin** adds 0–25% extra reduction, starting at 15%, according to how far the native corner speed falls below its maximum cap. Tighter upcoming bends receive more margin. The combined formula is `nativeCornerSpeed × baseFactor × (1 − margin/100 × (1 − nativeCornerSpeed/nativeMaximumSpeed))`. At 0%, it follows the v0.13 calculation exactly. With the strongest settings the effective factor can approach 0.45×; it never changes a straight-cap result. This adjusts the original planner’s speed cap, not its steering or proven sampling distance. Begin with normal 1× pace and power/grip changes off, comparing 0% and 15% on the same solo route.

It applies only to the current, owned AI driver's private main route in native free roam. Races, outruns, drag, drift and the Dyno Shop are excluded. Changing its enabled state, factor or sharp-turn margin rebuilds AI through a full native OFF/manual/ON handoff, because the game caches route speed caps. Free-roam/race transitions also rebuild before rearming.

**Corner status:** Armed means a request is present, not that a qualifying native reduction has been confirmed. Straight/gentle calls and guarded calls add no hit. Occupied command memory and observed drift exclusion are reported separately. The crash log now records bounded corner hits, request state, applied factor and those two observable guards. Confirmed pace is a different acknowledgment and does not prove corner assist ran. For diagnosis, use 1× pace; 0.95× corner factor reduces a qualifying corner cap by only 5%. A persistent no-hit result after bends is still unresolved without live telemetry.

It may help turn entry but cannot repair a bad route, prevent crashes, guarantee a clean corner or improve lap times. More power, grip or pace may undermine it. Live braking, route rebuilding and handling improvements remain unverified. Start conservatively and keep F7 available.

### Full per-race preset tuner

Use the **solo Performance Tuning main screen** on exact 93af6ccb. Back up your save, select a race preset in the game, then enable the tuner. It never buys upgrades, switches the game's preset, enters a race or presses Save Profile.

1. **Load selected preset** captures the current car, installed parts, working tune and selected visit tune on the game thread. The editor displays all 41 settings in their native categories and disables fields locked by installed parts/native rules.
2. Change sliders and press **Preview draft**. Native setters and rebuild/measurement functions run only in a separate memory copy. The preview shows accepted values, including native coupled changes, and comparable before/after estimates. Your live setup remains unchanged.
3. Alternatively choose a measured goal and press **Find tune**. Peak power/torque searches ECU/turbo; 0–60, 0–100 and top speed search gearing plus ECU/turbo. Search is capped at 48 trials. It keeps manual suspension, brake, tire, aero and NOS choices, but does not optimize their handling or lap-time effects. A faster estimated acceleration can reduce top speed; inspect all results.
4. **Stage selected preset** is an explicit separate action. It accepts only the last successfully evaluated candidate, on the same car, preset, installed parts and unchanged setup/visit/record. A game-thread transaction copies just the current 41-byte tune and selected 41-byte visit tune. Other presets and the saved-car record are not written by this action.
5. Start the game's own **Test Run** to refresh driving physics and check the tune. Merely exiting the tuning screen is not a verified rebuild. Use the game's **Save Profile** to persist changes. The game's save can commit all five visit presets, so the tuner warns when other visit presets differ from their stored record. “Save ready” is not a successful save confirmation.
6. **Restore previous** needs the same car, preset, parts and exact last-staged tune. It restores the original current and selected visit tunes, even when those originally differed. A known native commit of this exact selected tune is accepted; unrelated record changes are refused. Restore does not undo disk saves. Use Test Run and Save Profile again if you want the restored state refreshed and persisted.

Each car/preset has separate guarded restore state while the page stays open. A car replacement, manual edits, changed parts or an unknown record change invalidates stale results. Reload loses this temporary restore history. Native unlocked gear counts and tuning rules remain authoritative; no sixth gear is invented. Sliders display −100 to +100 around the game's neutral value, stored internally as bytes 0–200. These are normalized settings, not physical units.

The measurements are native estimates, not lap times or on-track benchmarks. Handling controls and NOS expose native settings without a proven per-race optimal objective. There are no claimed “perfect” race presets, global optimum, guaranteed wins or proven save/reload result. The previous peak-only dyno tool remains on older supported builds with its existing guarded Apply/Restore flow.

Cancel, F9, closing the panel, blur, a hidden tab, leaving the page or disabling the tuner cancels ongoing work. Driving effects pause during work, with their selections retained. **F9 does not undo a tune already staged.** Re-enable the tuner and use Restore previous while its baseline remains valid. A timed-out game-thread request has an uncertain outcome and disables further writes until reload; inspect the game rather than blindly retrying.

The private evaluator extracts only reviewed native functions from the exact game module already downloaded by the browser. It has its own memory, checked capture ranges, write allowlist and operation budget. Capture/stage/restore run through a command-gated frame prefix with no native calls and no profile-file writes. This bounds the reviewed path but is not a guarantee against browser exhaustion, unrelated game faults or live object-lifetime races.

### Power and handling

- **Unlimited NOS:** refills an already equipped kit while driving; does not install a kit or force native AI to activate NOS.
- **Power boost:** 1.0×–3.0× engine and nitrous torque. Starts at 1.5×. Repeated updates do not compound. More power can worsen wheelspin and handling.
- **Remove stock limiter:** removes the stock MPH governor while enabled. Gearing, drag and redline still limit speed. Upgraded cars may already lack that governor.
- **Extra grip:** 1.0×–2.0× all four tyre-force factors. Starts at 1.3×. It is not auto-steering, yaw damping, corner avoidance or guaranteed handling. High grip can cause abrupt behavior or rollover. It pauses in drift mode/races.
- Power and grip restore only fields still owned by the extension. They wait for three matching samples before applying to rebuilt car data. Changed external tuning is preserved rather than overwritten. Pause/off restores owned values when the original live objects remain valid.
- **Drift assist:** uses the game's real drift-event input and waits for its handling confirmation. Solo free roam only, with game menus closed. It is not perfect-drift automation. Power/grip restore before the native tuning rebuild; settings stay selected. Drift uses its own switch, including after F9.

### Wall / barrier pass-through

**Handling & collisions → Wall pass-through** is independent of AI and **solo-only**, even with Online/LAN tools allowed. Turn **Free roam with others** off, or use a solo race.

Only contacts between your car and verified near-vertical static track polygons are skipped, using the native wall threshold `abs(normal.z) < 0.1`. Ground, ceilings, ramps/slopes and movable props retain the original collision path. Cars retain it unless the independent Car no-clip option is enabled. Sloped faces and movable barrier props remain solid. This is not unrestricted flight or universal noclip. The game's native Ghost setting affects cars, not walls; the extension leaves that setting unchanged.

A selected checkbox is not proof of contact filtering. Its status first says Armed, then counts contacts actually skipped by the native hook. Test a plain vertical wall and neon barrier at low speed; verify ground/ramp and car collisions yourself. Coverage has not been live-verified.

You may leave the drivable map, miss checkpoints or get stuck inside scenery. Native recovery may reposition you after a reset. **Turn it off only when clear of a wall.** Off/F9/reload restores the original collision path. It does not change shared map objects or body collision flags.

### Solo Car no-clip

**Handling & collisions → Car no-clip** is separate from Wall pass-through and is solo-only. It matches confirmed native car collision bodies paired with the current local player's car, whether driven manually or by AI. It does not skip collisions between other cars. Walls, ground and props retain their normal path unless the wall option separately applies.

It starts off after reload and reports Armed until a supported contact is actually skipped. Turn it off only once clear of other cars. F9 stops it. No body flags or shared map objects are changed. Native constructor/category and current wrapper tests pass, but real traffic/racer collisions have not been live-verified.

### Online traffic no-clip

**Handling & collisions → Online traffic no-clip** is a separate switch, available on exact builds **93af6ccb and 78e2bb69**. It requires online free roam and matches native NPC traffic paired with your local car, driven manually or by AI. It excludes native player-slot cars even if they use a traffic model or traffic driver flag, plus ordinary AI racers, every race category, outruns and Online/LAN races. Other players and rejected contacts retain the game's original collision logic, including any native Ghost choice you made. Walls, ground, props, body flags and map objects are unchanged.

This switch starts **off after every reload**, even if previously selected. It needs its own explicit opt-in; **Allow Online/LAN tools** never enables it. That general permission is not required for this narrowly scoped online-free-roam traffic switch. Solo Car no-clip stays independent. The status distinguishes Armed from observed traffic contacts skipped. F9 stops and clears it; blur, hidden tabs, dyno work and unavailable driving state pause it. Turn it off only when clear of traffic.

No live online collisions, peer synchronization or server acceptance have been verified. It changes local contact resolution, not the traffic simulation or server rules. Follow the site's rules and use an explicitly permitted private test. A selected or Armed switch is not proof that a real contact was skipped.

### Manual drag assist

A separate, optional throttle / RPM-threshold shift / NOS helper **while you steer**. Uses default Arrow Up, Left Shift and Left Alt bindings. Set shift RPM for your car; 6500 is only a starting point, not learned perfect shifting.

Manual drag assist never runs while automatic drag AI is requested, including countdown and failed/unavailable AI. It will not silently substitute synthetic inputs. With Automatic AI off, manual drag waits for native ownership to clear and a human driver to be confirmed. Countdown permits throttle only; shifts and NOS wait for GO. It does not choose lanes or avoid obstacles. F7/manual takeover pauses it until its switch is toggled again.

### Diagnostics

#### Local crash log

Open **Driving tools → Session & diagnostics → Crash log → Export crash log**. This downloads `nfsu2-driving-tools-diagnostics.json` on your computer. Nothing is automatically sent or uploaded. **Clear log** removes this tab's retained diagnostic history; recording then continues.

The logger starts when this extension page loads. It records recent tool choices/factors, sampled game mode and driver state, page/game-worker lifecycle, classified errors, numeric WebAssembly function/offset locations and line numbers from known script files. It does not capture raw console logs, error messages, URLs, credentials, names, saves, keyboard input or network traffic. It never changes game memory or enables a tool.

The newest **180 events, limited to 64 KiB of stored JSON**, are kept in same-tab session storage. State is sampled on discrete changes (at most four times a second), moving native scalars about every two seconds, and a baseline snapshot every five seconds while driving; rapid repeated page errors are capped. Older entries are discarded and the file reports the count. Export soon after a problem. Reloading the same tab normally retains the log; closing the tab, clearing site data, browser recovery behavior or blocked/full storage can lose it. The menu reports when the log is memory-only. The site's own scripts can access this same-origin session storage, so it is not an extension-private vault.

**Capture limits:** this cannot recover crashes that happened before the logger was installed. A full browser/tab/GPU crash, freeze or forced close may prevent any final event. This is a history of observations, not a complete crash dump or proof of the crash's cause; the last snapshot may precede the failure. Free-text errors are deliberately omitted for privacy, so unfamiliar errors appear as `other`. Also export the game's own **Download log** for native game details. This logger does not fix the reported crash or establish that the game is safe.


The read-only traffic/barrier tester reads nearby car objects and the enabled barrier-line table. It is incomplete: it does not fully classify traffic/racers, shapes, props, road geometry, elevation or safe lanes. No detected obstacle does not imply a safe road.

## Online / LAN

Online/LAN remains blocked by default for existing tools. The separate **Session mode → Allow Online/LAN tools** switch is per-page and starts off on reload. It does not activate individual tools. It never overrides the solo restrictions on walls and solo Car no-clip, drag physics requirements, pause checks or one-local-player checks. Online traffic no-clip remains online-free-roam-only. Current-build Online player / race no-clip requires its own selection plus network permission for the race path; only local contacts are affected.

Online modifications may affect racers, trigger integrity checks, invalidate results or cause moderation/bans. Follow the site's rules and prefer solo play or an explicitly permitted private test. This extension does not bypass server restrictions. Turning off the session switch stops AI/synthetic keys and restores owned tuning when possible, while keeping selections for solo. NOS already refilled is not drained. F9 clears the permission.

## Validation and known limits

**Automated validation:** the final v0.28 suite passes **1,740 tests, zero failures/skips/cancellations**, including high-address runtime CPU cases. See `CHANGELOG.md`. The frozen v0.20 tuner baseline passed 1,599 tests. Coverage includes the retained v0.18 regressions, actual native isolated getter/setter/rebuild and metrics, all unlocked control offsets, exact game-thread capture/stage/restore, all five preset leases, stale-state/identity/cancellation/fuel guards, and end-to-end private preview with selected-preset-only writes. The end-to-end harness uses exact native game functions and a constructed car/catalog fixture, not a live user's game. Focused suites overlap and are not additive totals. These checks are not a full game simulation or live gameplay.

All four exact supported modules validate and compile after patching. Both modern profiles change12 bodies: **2459, 3174, 4497, 4653, 7395, 8871, 17404, 19197, 19277, 21213, 21263**, plus contact wrapper **22508** on93af6ccb or **22470** on78e2bb69. On2f0ddd3b, only **4497, 4653, 21213, 21262 and22430** change; on6f4f1e4e, only **4497, 4653, 21213, 21262 and22720** change. Every other function body and non-code section is preserved byte-for-byte. Original planner instructions and contact-wrapper tails remain preserved. The native Drift recovery expression replacement retains its documented scope. Authored builders reproduce the shipped payloads.

No successful live drag race, wall/car test, cornering improvement, real-car dyno improvement or online race is claimed. The menu passes simulated DOM checks. The strict-CSP Chromium regression test could not run because this environment blocks Chromium startup; no real-browser visual verification is claimed.

The v0.11 crash remains undiagnosed. Controlled interleaving tests did expose stale-state and competing-writer hazards in power, grip and NOS. This release rechecks live state/identity at each field, uses exact-value atomic updates/restoration, rejects out-of-domain power values and avoids unchanged-value rewrites. These are experimental mitigations, not full lifetime synchronization: the native game can still destroy/reuse an object before updating its pointer. No elimination of that residual race or the reported freezes is claimed. The current game-thread gcall ABI, dispatch mapping and hook-local layout match the reviewed native binary; that does not establish the absence of timing, lifetime or gameplay faults. Stop using a feature if the game becomes unstable, preserve the crash log and reload before retesting.

Exact supported profiles:

- **93af6ccb:** 38,205,596 bytes, SHA-256 `128e2b5816a8eace4b768aec920318a1613da8235801a361e2009e96550be1d6`. Newest reviewed profile, with the64-entry native status table and all current controls.
- **78e2bb69:** 38,170,601 bytes, SHA-256 `df7b930bb293ffdf975f0735d93e0797d51bd137d0cbeabcaff87fc5a693c759`. Previous reviewed modern profile. Main hook 21213, dispatch 21726, gcall 21740, pace wrapper 21263, contact wrapper 22470; exact native bodies and relocated wrappers are checked offline.

The native gcall function was mapped from old index 21725 to current index 21739 and verified to preserve the same CPU ABI; actual dispatch tables and native AI bodies were checked independently.
- **6f4f1e4e:** 37,839,055 bytes, SHA-256 `ee5d281a3109240d5db25dc3921e1044672cf6d650eb58c3baa089b54fe2941f`. Retains the older combined experimental feature set.

An independent probe executes actual current-build input/status initialization, status writing and the NOS reader in isolated memory: 22 assertions pass. This verifies the mailbox formats and NOS interpretation, not a real gameplay session. A separate native gcall binary comparison verifies that its only body change is the dispatcher call relocation.

## Privacy, implementation and rollback

The extension matches only `https://nfsu2.xyz/*`. No account, history, debugger or broad website permissions. It stores its own preferences and a bounded, sanitized diagnostic history in namespaced same-tab session-storage entries. Nothing is uploaded. Its only added request is a same-origin `/game.json` compatibility read; it inspects the game's own module response during loading. No analytics, remote code or game assets are bundled.

- AI calls native `Player::AutoPilotOn`, `AutoPilotOff` and `SetInputMode` through the game's existing CPU-preserving game-thread dispatcher. It never invokes native game functions concurrently from the page thread.
- Normal drag opponents use driver type 3 / physics type 1, while player autopilot initially asks for physics type 3. The retained drag handoff corrects only the eligible local car, verifies both types and rolls back on failure.
- The page's automatic AI switch supplies the exact drag-permission word only when drag is detected. The native permission and full-physics checks are still required. The pace hook never modifies drag.
- Mode switching publishes OFF and verifies the native heartbeat acknowledgement, cleared ownership and restored manual driver before rearming. Identity, native subtype/track flags and race/free-roam mode are part of that comparison. Native Off/On rebuilds the private driver route.
- Command memory stays at `0x00d0d100` (104 bytes used on modern Drag-heat profiles;92 bytes on older profiles) and walls at `0x00d0d180` (40 bytes), under sequence locks. Cars use `0x00d0d1c0` (40 bytes); the existing final word selects the independent online traffic/player modes on 93af6ccb and 78e2bb69. The corner record is at `0x00d0d200` (64 bytes, CNR3), and dyno uses `0x00d0d300..0x00d0d4ff`. These do not overlap. Native scalar-reference/allocator analysis supports using these gaps, but exclusive allocation has not been formally proved and unknown computed writes remain a risk. Cold empty/owned checks and post-attachment ownership guards reduce, not eliminate, that risk. The current-build patch targets the main-loop bridge, player pace, contact resolver, corner/braking helpers, native drag action/input selectors, native Drift damping expression and three guarded nitrous acceptance sites. Original native instructions remain preserved around the scoped changes.
- The full tuner additionally grows the game memory by an owned 16 MiB snapshot buffer, records its module/memory identity and uses the existing dyno mailbox for commands. Snapshot growth is not undone until reload. Native evaluation runs in separate memory with guarded reads/writes and execution fuel. Staging does not call a game physics rebuild or save helper.
- Wall filtering prefixes `sub_005b2610` and preserves the full original resolver for every rejected contact. Body type/vtable, reciprocal car/face pointers, finite unit normals and pair identities are checked. Native `roam_game_online_here()` always blocks wall filtering during multiplayer free roam. The separate latest-build traffic path also calls the exact native read-only player-slot helper and excludes recognized player cars.

For rollback, disable v0.29.0, enable your preserved previous version and reload. The previous version remains subject to its own build-compatibility checks. Memory effects do not survive reload; saved ordinary preferences may. Never run both versions together.

# Adaptive corner-speed candidate

Separate candidate based on `combined-v013`. The original baseline is unchanged. No live-game result is claimed. This change is ready for code integration/testing, not a claim of improved route following.

## Finding

The existing helper already receives upcoming route-point curvature and its reduced speed is consumed by the native route braking calculations. Its old modifier was constant. The new modifier adds a bounded, continuous margin as the native curvature-limited speed drops farther below the native maximum:

```
severity = 1 - nativeCornerSpeed / nativeMaximumSpeed
plannedSpeed = nativeCornerSpeed * baseFactor * (1 - marginPercent / 100 * severity)
```

This runs only after the original function has calculated a finite positive curvature-limited output strictly below the cap. Thus `0 < severity < 1`, and the additional multiplier lies between 0.75 and 1. Margin 0 takes the exact previous multiplication path. The base factor remains 0.60–0.95. Combined output can approach 0.45× native output with the strongest settings. Gentle/straight caps, invalid inputs, unowned routes, other cars, race/outrun/drag/dyno cases and all prior guards retain native behavior.

The UI adds **Sharp-turn margin**, 0–25%, default 15%, in 5% steps. Assist remains off after reload. API default is 0 for compatibility with callers that do not explicitly opt into the new margin. Turning the margin to 0 restores the v0.13 calculation. Changing active factor/margin goes through the existing full OFF/manual/ON route rebuild. Disabled margin changes do not trigger needless rebuilds.

Example, g=1, cap=60, base factor 0.80, margin 15%:

- Curvature 0.003: native 57.1548; old cap 45.7238; adaptive cap about 45.3986.
- Curvature 0.01: native 31.3050; old cap 25.0440; adaptive cap about 23.2473.
- Curvature 0.10: native 9.8995; old cap 7.9196; adaptive cap about 6.9277.

Values use the native helper's speed units. These synthetic outputs are not measured gameplay performance.

## What this does not do

This does not extend a proven forward-lookahead distance, change steering, identify walls/traffic, repair bad paths or guarantee collision-free driving. The apparent 10/20-node constant in native 0x428030 was deliberately not changed: following its exact control flow shows it subtracted from the current node before route maintenance, which does not establish a forward sampling horizon. Calling it a safe lookahead knob would overstate the evidence.

The original native planner still decides which points to sample and how to propagate acceleration/deceleration. Lower corner caps are intended to make its existing anticipation more conservative. Strong custom pace, power and handling can undermine the result. Test first with normal 1× pace, power/grip changes off, solo free roam, and a backed-up save. Compare the same route/car with margin 0%, then 15%; use F7 if behavior deteriorates. No extension controls were installed or changed in a live browser here.

## Implementation

- `extension/ai.js`: margin publishing, changed-profile handback, actual effective-cap diagnostics, 44-byte cold ownership check.
- `tools/build-corner-hook.cjs`: authored postlude only. Original native instructions remain contiguous and unchanged; no additional patched function or pointer traversal.
- `tools/corner-hook.{json,wat}`: generated payload/source.
- `extension/page.js`: adjustable margin, retention, explanatory text, accessible percent value.
- `extension/diagnostics.js`: bounded margin field in existing sanitized logs.
- Three native/profile test suites, three controller/profile suites, and page wiring tests exercise the addition.

Corner command identity changes from CNR1 to CNR2, rejecting stale/occupied records. Memory is `0xd0d200..0xd0d22b` (44 bytes), before dyno at `0xd0d300`. +36 is requested margin percent; +40 echoes the applied margin. Existing +20/+24 native/output speed diagnostics report the actual last effective multiplier. Zero margin retains legacy factor reporting. Both factor and margin echoes must match the current command before a hit can confirm application.

The extension directory still identifies itself as v0.13.0 because this is an integration candidate, not a separately released build. Update release naming/version only during final combined packaging. Do not ship tests, extracted native Wasm, or research files.

## Validation results

- `node --test tests/*.test.cjs`: **472 tests pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped**. This includes all three exact supported native helper profiles, unchanged-body/section checks, complete patched module validation/compilation, and the added native/controller/UI tests.
- `node tools/build-corner-hook.cjs` reproduces the embedded payload, JSON and WAT byte-for-byte.
- `node --check` passes for all extension JavaScript and the modified builder.
- Full test output is retained in `validation/adaptive-corner-tests.txt` (developer evidence only; exclude from release ZIP).
- Real-browser visual testing and live-gameplay testing were **not run**. No proof of collision reduction or better steering is claimed.

## Evidence and limits

# Isolated road-race hairpin candidate

This directory is a separate copy of combined-v017. No shipped files, installed settings or live game were changed. Version metadata is intentionally unchanged for the parent release integrator. This is experimental native-planner tuning, not a measured racing improvement.

## Behavior

- Independent Road-race hairpin assist, OFF by default and after reload/Stop.
- Solo ordinary race category1 with HUD/mode1 only. Drag, drift, their forced flags, outrun, dyno and network play are excluded. General Online/LAN permission does not enable this first race option.
- Retains the native driver, racing line, checkpoints, recovery, opponents and original function instructions. It does not add steering, collision avoidance, route nodes or a longer verified horizon.
- Race corner factor0.6–0.95 (default0.8), sharp-turn margin0–25% (default15), planning braking factor0.5–1 (default0.75). Lower braking factor means a more conservative native braking assumption, not weaker physical brakes.
- Existing free-roam corner behavior/calculation remains separate and unchanged. Its old high-pace interaction is not silently changed by the race option.
- Straight race pace selection remains independent. No nitro or grip change is included.

## Native implementation

The existing4653 curvature helper pre/post hook recognizes separate command2. Its verified call from0x422780 has return0x4228bb, EBX=owned car and ESI=owned current private main route (driver+0x370 == *(driver+0x6e8)). Existing command1 retains the free-roam calculation.

For command2 with selected pace P=max(1,percent/100), the upcoming curvature threshold uses paced cap P*C. The helper recomputes the unbounded curvature limit from validated g and curvature when P>1, applies the bounded corner factor/adaptive margin, then divides its apex result by P. Non-limiting straight cases retain their native cap. This counteracts the existing later custom-pace multiplication without lowering a clear straight's cap.

New pre/post hook4497 scales the native planning deceleration by braking/P². It allows only:

1. Main corner-planner getter return0x4227a1, ESI=private route and EBX=owned car.
2. Backward propagation getter return0x40a723, EBP=private route, BL=0, outer return at getterSP+40=0x422b2e, direction atSP+48=0 and matching car argument atSP+52.

All shared grade-table contents and other getter calls are untouched. Native forward acceleration uses its original evaluator. Both hooks check fresh command identity, stable even sequence, ownership, player, car, driver, mode, race, solo context and bounded settings; original instructions remain contiguous. No original game code is embedded in the extension.

For a synthetic route, the compensated final target is equivalent to:

`min(P*C, sqrt(V² + 2*a*braking*distance))`

Native difficulty/catchup factors and physical handling still exist. This is not a claim that3x target yields3x actual speed or that a short route horizon supports safe high-speed driving.

## Command record and lifecycle

CNR3 marker0x33524e43,64-byte record at0xd0d200. Previous fields retain meaning; added:

- +44: requested braking percent50–100.
- +48: requested selected pace percent75–300, must equal AI command+60.
- +52: corner helper pace echo.
- +56: corner helper braking echo.
- +60: actual eligible braking-getter count, separate from corner hits.

Older markers or occupied expanded bytes are never overwritten. Controller bounds and cold native mailbox guards cover the full64 bytes. Both corner settings and effective selected race pace changes perform the existing successful OFF/manual/ON handback, rebuilding cached private route caps. Stops, profile changes and ownership changes clear diagnostic echoes/counts. Merely changing the selected straight pace with race assistance disabled does not rebuild.

Reachability diagnostics from corner-reachability-v017 are included. Negative stage values occupy the old curvature diagnostic word only until the first actual corner hit. Braking hits alone never confirm a corner adjustment. Page status and logs include cornerMode, selected cornerPace, cornerBraking and brakingHits; counters do not claim better live handling.

## Rebuild

From this candidate directory, set WABT_MODULE to the existing research/compatibility-v011/node_modules/wabt if needed, then run:

- node tools/build-corner-hook.cjs
- node tools/build-braking-hook.cjs
- node tools/build-current-profile.cjs
- node tools/build-latest-profile.cjs
- node tools/build-next-profile.cjs

The current-profile builder expands the cold mailbox guard and regenerates the base used by the later profiles. Preserve unrelated drag/diagnostics/grip candidates when integrating; merge authored source changes rather than overwriting their generated profile files.

## Validation and limits

See the final parent handoff for exact test totals. New tests exercise actual hash-pinned native helpers/propagation, race guards, cached-route handback, request/echo distinction, unchanged disabled/forward paths, complete-memory write boundaries, exact module compilation and original-instruction containment. Page tests cover default/reset state and independent controls.

No browser driving, live collision count, race time, placement, grip benefit or nitro behavior was measured. Native route records/horizon may still miss a particular hairpin. Exact180-degree degenerate three-point geometry can return zero curvature; this candidate does not invent a geometry fallback without route evidence. Keep the prior release as the rollback baseline. Do not package research, extracted native assets, tests or tools in an extension ZIP.

# v0.33 Continuous sampled-corner release

Frozen source: `combined-v033-integration`, based on frozen `combined-v032-integration`.

## Deliverable

User archive: `NFSU2-Driving-Tools-v0.33-Desktop-Folder.zip`.
- 238,099 bytes.
- SHA-256: `06bf5f37ddfd446ba845813b23fa376bb6c41719c038aa85b65f80aa839b5b28`.
- Library ID: `libfile_fde3_f-8f11c3be28888191918b5120d21e4740_8b516292de4881919d77c9d94b12acf3`.
- File ID: `file_00000000f0c081f5ae49e658bdbe1b23`; version 0. Local identity applied; post-upload hash unchanged.
- Exactly one stable inner folder, `NFSU2-Driving-Tools`, containing the 26 release files. No game modules, extracted game code, research inputs, tests or tools are packaged.

First install: extract the ZIP, drag the actual folder onto Desktop and Load unpacked once. For an existing install, replace files inside the exact folder already loaded by the browser, Reload that existing extension card and refresh the game. Do not replace the extension identity or silently relocate it. Verify version 0.33.0. The ZIP itself does not run.

Internal reproduction archive: `NFSU2-Driving-Tools-v0.33-Combined-Continuous-Corners.zip`, 234,522 bytes, SHA-256 `effa0eeea59f81f978a577018eaf9542f9d5c8c8e10323ad308c46b9aba2785c`. Do not deliver this versioned-folder archive instead of the requested Desktop-folder package.

## Integrated scope

Reviewed input: `continuous-corners-v033-candidate/integration/continuous-corners/continuous-corners.patch`, SHA-256 `e984c2247775cb3a2fb276add05ea6da31405042593170d0a8a12e8070851f59`.

A new guarded command 3 is used only by the existing optional adaptive road mode. It replaces the old curvature threshold with a smooth bounded target for valid sampled nonzero native bends; the native backward planner uses matching pace compensation. Exact straights, native lower/stop results and old command 1/2 behavior are preserved. Actual/forced/known-online Street X is excluded in both native wrappers, while the controller retains Street X's existing selections.

Existing ownership, current identities, network opt-in, native handback, sequence, watchdog and race guards remain. No added steering, physical brake writes, route horizon, shifting, NOS actions, collision behavior, saves or profile schema change. New modes remain default-off/session-only and no existing values are silently changed.

Corner/braking hit counts use the existing two-second telemetry interval rather than causing quarter-second history churn. Discrete changes still log promptly. UI/log evidence is historical hook activity, not confirmation the current turn is safe.

All v0.32 features are retained: race-only AI, tuner/static-ride fix, NOS correction, Drag protection/retention, profiles, online controls, HUD, F8/Shift+Insert/F7/F9. Unrelated Drag lane and hosted-race candidates and unverified grip/downforce are not integrated. Autonomous lobby research remains separate.

## Verification

- Complete final combined suite: **1,942 passed, zero failures/skips/cancellations** (`all-tests-final.txt`).
- Desktop-folder builder suite: **31 passed** (`folder-builder-tests.txt`).
- All four pinned native modules compile; only function 4497 (braking wrapper) and function 4653 (curvature wrapper) differ from v0.32. Exact outputs match the reviewed authored candidate (`module-delta.json`).
- Reviewed authored runtime matches exactly except release version strings; 19 source/tool/test files changed from v0.32 and 199 preserved (`preservation.json`). Metadata/docs are the only additional release changes.
- Frozen v0.32 source matches its immutable original release archive; original versioned and flat archives retain their hashes.
- Complete integration patch plus seven builders reproduces all 19 changed files and the internal release ZIP exactly (`integrated-v033.patch`, `reproduce.py`, `reproduction-results.json`).
- Root's prior independent authored review passed 117 focused tests and four module checks. The final independent integration review passed 222 focused tests, independently reran the complete 1,942-test aggregate and 31 packaging tests, and found no delivery blocker. It verified all four module outputs, source preservation, syntax, checksum/CRC/manifest integrity, repeatable Desktop-folder builds and simulated repeat overlay. Evidence and final report are in `research/continuous-corners-merge-v033/`.
- The delivery archive independently reproduces byte-for-byte twice; all runtime files match frozen source, with the builder's documented installation README and two packaging files as the only packaging additions. All 218 candidate source/tool/test file hashes stayed unchanged throughout final review.

## Limits

This fixes a supported threshold gap for sampled bends, not missing native corner records, skipped route-tail entries, zero-curvature inputs, auxiliary routes or steering errors. It is not complete all-map corner detection or a proven cure for every reported missed turn. High pace remains risky. Prior logs establish active settings/hook observations but not one common cause. Live gameplay, successful turns, race outcomes, browser appearance and game save persistence were not verified. No live user game actions were taken.

+# v0.33.0 · Continuous adaptive targets for sampled bends
+
+- Optional adaptive road mode now uses a separate guarded native command with a smooth bounded curvature target for each valid sampled nonzero bend. Exact straights and existing lower/stop results retain native behavior. Distance-based braking uses the same pace compensation.
+- Preserves Street X in the page, controller and both native guards. Existing free-roam and road-corner commands retain exact prior behavior. Default-off/session-only choices, current sliders, online opt-in, ownership, handback and watchdog remain unchanged.
+- This addresses the old curvature threshold, not missing native corner records, skipped route tails, zero-curvature data, auxiliary routes or steering. It does not provide all-map corner detection or a guarantee of clean turns or wins. Live gameplay remains unverified.
+- Corner/braking counters use the existing two-second telemetry cadence to retain more useful history. Discrete control/mode changes still log promptly; hook hits do not verify the current corner.
+- Combined suite: **1,942 passed, zero failures/skips/cancellations**. All four pinned modules compile; only functions 4497 and 4653 differ from v0.32. Retains tuner, NOS, Drag retention/protection, saved profiles, race-only AI, HUD and shortcuts. No unrelated lane/hosted-race candidate or unverified grip/downforce activation.

+## v0.33.0: Continuous adaptive corner targets
+
+Adaptive road-race speed now has a separate native planning command. Every valid sampled nonzero bend receives a smooth curvature-based target, instead of requiring it to cross the older curvature threshold. Exact straights keep the requested target ceiling; existing native lower/stop results are never increased. The native distance-based braking calculation uses the same pace compensation.
+
+The curve is deliberately conservative and experimental. It does not detect every corner on the map: the native planner may provide no corner records, skip a tail record, report zero curvature or use another route. It does not change steering, physical brakes, route lookahead, NOS or other cars. A hook hit is an observation of a past call, not proof the current corner is safe. Five fresh captures show hook hits despite reported missed turns, so the update is not presented as a proven fix for every failure.
+
+Only adaptive road mode uses this new command. **Street X and existing free-roam/road-corner controls retain their exact prior behavior.** The new command also denies actual/forced Street X and known online Street X in its native guards. AI ownership, native handback, online permission, mode checks and watchdog remain required. This does not bypass an AI failure or acquire control automatically.
+
+The option remains default-off/session-only and uses your current sliders without changing saved values. For the first comparison, try the existing defaults: 1.30× adaptive ceiling, 0.80 corner factor and 0.75 braking factor. Higher targets can still cause missed turns. The latest logs used 1.90×, 0.95 and 1.00 respectively; those settings were confirmed, not shown to be safe. Keep the working Street X setup unchanged.
+
+Corner/braking hit counters now use the existing two-second telemetry sample cadence instead of replacing bounded history every quarter second. Discrete control/mode changes still log promptly. No raw route geometry, memory dump or additional personal data is collected.
+
+Native tests execute the new corner and braking hooks against the pinned game routines, compare legacy commands byte-for-byte, and check protected outputs and guard denials. Live cornering, race results and browser rendering remain unverified. The final combined suite passes **1,942 tests, zero failures/skips/cancellations**. # Drag native input handoff, 93af6ccb

## Diagnosis

The released v0.17 path calls Player::AutoPilotOn (0x5fae20) directly. This replaces the driver with3 but does not change current input mode Player+0x22c or requested input mode Player+0x230. Exact native Player::Update (0x602650, Wasm8414) calls 0x5f3010 when current input mode3 is inconsistent with a non-2 driver. That function replaces the just-acquired driver3 with manual drag driver2. This reproduces the user's short driver3/owned sample followed by driver2/unowned without any heartbeat failure.

A SetInputMode4-only repair is insufficient. Player::Update invokes native drag-mode selection0x5f39d0 (Wasm19197) after that driver check. It writes requested mode3 when the player is moving in the relevant drag context. Native input reconciliation0x5ea650 (Wasm4344) derives current mode from requested mode and invokes SetInputMode0x605c70 (Wasm14982). Requested4 thus becomes3 and native AI is relinquished. Function0x600f30 is a queued relocation handler, not input reconciliation.

The normal native UI/debug request path at0x603327 cycles requested2→4→5→2. Mode4 is the game's native AutoPilot input mode. SetInputMode unregisters old callback bindings; mode4 invokes AutoPilotOn. Leaving mode4 invokes AutoPilotOff and registers the destination mode. Calling On/Off separately does not provide this full input lifecycle.

## Narrow repair

The new isolated `drag-input-handoff-v018` candidate changes only modern reviewed78e2bb69 and93af6ccb profiles:

- Acquire only an ordinary local player record, ready Drag car with full physics1, a live permission/heartbeat lease, native manual driver1 or2, and current/requested manual input modes2/3.
- Save requested2/3 in existing reserved mailbox B+96, mark a native mode lease at B+92, request4 once, and call native SetInputMode4. Existing post-On physics1 correction and opponent goal2 selection remain in place.
- Prefix only native drag manual-mode selection0x5f39d0. It returns early solely for its exact Player-update caller return0x602ab4 and independently verified owned local player/car/race/driver, mode4/request4, physics1, ordinary record, active race4, runtime permission, Drag opt-in, stable even sequence and fresh heartbeat. Network guards remain unless explicitly allowed. The guard performs no steering, throttle, goal, skill, driver-kind or input-mode writes. It only performs the native no-argument return when qualified.
- Do not alter native input reconciliation or the complete Player update. A real native mode/request change ends the lease and latches reacquisition until an explicit OFF cycle, rather than fighting the game.
- Handback restores the saved request only if it is still our4. A newer request is preserved. SetInputMode exits4 via original Off exactly once. A newer current mode and its controller are likewise preserved. The actual native4→5 path is exercised: its Off→On creates a new native driver3; extension invalidation does not call Off again or replace that driver. Existing skill compare-and-restore remains unchanged.
- Recognize native manual driver2 through local-player/manual input-mode checks even while Drag flags are transitioning. A foreign/scripted driver is not reported as a completed manual handback.
- Reserve B+92..99 in first-handshake occupancy checks. No other mailbox gap is consumed.

The repair is gated on the actual Drag byte0x89e7d8. Force-Drag-only (0x890108 set with that byte clear) is left on the prior native path and is not covered by this repair or its live-log diagnosis. No debug-mode expansion was made.

This deliberately does not acquire during countdown/race phase3. It still waits for phase4/GO and does not establish optimal launch RPM, launch timing or race-winning performance.

## Verification and limits

`probe-native-input.cjs` reads SHA-256-pinned current game code at runtime. It executes the exact original Player::Update, native drag selection, input reconciliation, SetInputMode, On, Off and both manual-driver-switch bodies. Production-authored guard bytes are grafted onto the exact native drag selection body. Numeric mapping to the original named routines is checked by `mapping.json`, allowing only enumerated host dispatch/helper relocations.

The probe reproduces both the legacy loss and the failure of mode4 without retention. The guarded mode4 path survives180 full Player updates plus native reconciliations. A second180-cycle test connects the actual production bridge to the native lifecycle bodies, observes actual skill9 retained, and confirms no repeated driver reconstruction. Native manual handback reaches driver2/physics1/current3/request3. OFF, opt-out, pause, requested manual/special modes, native driver replacement, native mode replacement and heartbeat expiry restore saved skill4. An intervening skill6 is neither forced back to9 nor overwritten on release.33 rejected guard cases have byte-exact native fallback; other caller sites retain the original behavior. Foreign/scripted modes cannot be acquired.

The fixture controls allocator/physics-switch and callback-registration leaves and unrelated subsystems. It does not execute a complete visual game, simulate the driver AI's entire action-update graph, or prove a race finish. Opponent goal2 selection is separately tested by the existing exact native initializer suites; this Player-update replay proves ownership/input retention and does not claim full goal2 behavioral retention across all recovery/events. Goal/null/recovery pointers are explicitly unchanged by the new guard. Live driving validation remains necessary.

No original game binary, disassembly or extracted function should be included in an extension release. The shipped patch contains authored guard/bridge instructions only and fails closed on an unknown module hash.

# v0.24 combined online Drag candidate

Outcome: locally validated and independently reviewed. Live online race behavior remains unverified.

## Artifact

`NFSU2-Driving-Tools-v0.24-Combined-Online-Drag-Tuner.zip` is 204,573 bytes. SHA-256: `eaf1745261a9da590890433503fc57460546459e3045c2a5af34fc6731ad4a9e`.

Library ID: `libfile_fde3_f-411d53689838819186fbf7c98ebb709e_8b516292de4881919d77c9d94b12acf3`.

## Changes

- Extends the corrected v0.23 heat-only protection to online/LAN only with literal network permission. The UI requires both Disable Drag engine blowouts and Allow network tools. Independent manual operation remains possible.
- Retains every native ownership, identity, active Drag, full physics, finite/unblown heat, epoch and heartbeat check. High-address runtime CPU validation remains corrected. The only extension write is current local engine heat to the native disabled sentinel.
- All unrelated profile fields/capabilities, full-tuner prefix, contacts, Street X, corner and braking payloads remain unchanged. No Lap Knockout or unverified native grip/downforce activation. Native NOS, shifting, throttle, steering and opponents are unchanged.
- Corrects test snapshots to copy bytes instead of aliasing the same memory.

## Verification

- Final aggregate suite: 1,669 passed, zero failures, skips or cancellations. `all-tests-final.txt`.
- Independent native review: 15 check groups, plus 44 heat tests. `research/drag-overheat-online-v024/REVIEW.md` and its output files.
- Both exact pinned native modules survive 600 online redline frames at low/high runtime CPU addresses. Opt-out resumes native heating and blowout. Rejected online permission, stale, opponent and invalid states match original native behavior.
- Independent frozen ZIP check: 23 entries exactly match final sources; CRC clean; no extra, missing or duplicate entries; manifest 0.24.0 and reviewed runtime hashes unchanged. Final reviewer reran all 44 heat tests.
- Source patch applies to frozen v0.23 without conflicts. Three builders reproduce all 18 changed files and the byte-identical ZIP. See `integrated-v024.patch`, `reproduce.py`, `changed-files.json`, `reproduction-results.json`.

## Limits and operating instructions

Reload with only v0.24 enabled, enable both named toggles before a fresh online Drag race and before damage. Already-blown engines or lost races are not repaired. An enabled checkbox is a request, not proof that native eligibility guards passed. Observe the bounded heat diagnostics in a fresh race for end-to-end confirmation. The reported network=true log explains why solo-only v0.23 would reject the request; it does not prove every native guard passes in the live game.

This is not a repeated-NOS fix, guaranteed win or peer/server behavior guarantee. Follow server rules. No installation, browser/HUD verification, live online race or save/reload test was performed. The full tuner remains a 41-field manual editor and private native preview with measured gearing/ECU/turbo searches, not automatic handling/lap optimization. Game Test Run and Save Profile are still required for physics refresh and persistence; disk save is not confirmed by the extension.
